page.layout: One printed page: running text in a single column; one marginal note in the left margin beside the paragraph about the Huns' invasion of Pannonia. The strip of text at the right edge belongs to the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: tilæ; instrumentalis: plurimæ natio-nes potentes, Gothi, Gepidæ, Lon-gobardi, qvæ singulæ rebellarunt. Qvapropter Chaba, Attilæ filius natu major, cùm vidisset rem desperatam, reliqvias Hunnorum in Scythiam reduxit, paucis ultrò remanentibus, qvi, ne Hunnorum nomine suspecti essent, Siculos se appellarunt, & itahodieq; in Transylvania appel-lantur. Significat autem Siculorum nomen lingvâ Hunnicâ reliqvias.
main_text.head: Periodus III.
Can. I.
Ugri Hunnis in Pannoniâ successerunt.
Explicatio 1.
main_text.p: Facta qvidem fuit secunda Hun-norum in Pannoniam irruptio A. C. 744, qvo sub VII. Ducibus exercitu 200000 militum in Pannonias ve-nerunt: contra qvos Carolus M. & alii Imperatores Francorum magna belladenuò irrumpunt in Pannoniam,

page.notes: The first word of the page, "tilæ", is a fragment of a word continued from the previous page and is kept as printed. The marginal note at left is set in a smaller roman type. The word "successerunt" is printed with a long s and read as such. The paragraph ends at "bella", which continues on the next page. "Periodus" is not in the list of division words; it is treated as a level-1 division because it is a numbered part heading. No catchword or signature is visible.
